prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: GLP-1 is the one candidate that all six of us ranked first, and that agreement rests on substance rather than convenience. The arc runs from incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, through identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to receptor agonists with durable effects on glycemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, confirmed in many large independent trials across several drug classes. The discovery is original, the mechanism is clear, and the human impact is very large and still growing. A single-achievement prize with Holst for physiology, Drucker for biology and therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov for the active peptide form is the most defensible configuration from the supplied credit list.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness. Three slots cannot cover the discovery side (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, and Habener who is not on our list) and the development side (Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues made the drugs). Mojsov's credit for the active peptide is contested. If we judge that the clinical transformation is inseparable from the industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, the discovery-only trio is arguably incomplete and could be criticised as honouring the mechanism while omitting the people who made it a medicine.

responses.point: Ranked TNF blockade (B036, Feldmann and Maini) second as a clean bench-to-bedside discovery that has spread across immune-mediated disease, fully mature and already Lasker-recognised.
responses.response: I agree the attribution is cleaner than for most candidates, and the maturity is not in doubt. My hesitation is novelty of principle compared with CAR-T. TNF blockade validated a cytokine as a therapeutic target in an established disease, whereas engineered T cells created a new class of living drug. I also worry the translational claim is shared with antibody-engineering and cloning groups outside the pair. I keep B036 below my top choices but would not oppose it if the committee prefers a compact two-person immunology prize.

responses.point: Placed TOR/mTOR (B004) second, with Hall's genetic identification of TOR in yeast as the decisive step, and included Sabatini and Schreiber as co-recipients.
responses.response: I share the view that Hall's step is decisive and that the biology is conceptually unifying. I disagree on adding Sabatini. The three-person limit and the unresolved questions about his standing make a Hall and Schreiber core safer, and even that pair leaves the mammalian target and complex discoveries to be allocated. My larger reservation is that clinical impact, outside transplantation and a few cancers, is much narrower than the basic biology, so I rank it below CAR-T and imatinib.

responses.point: Ranked optogenetics (B018) second, arguing it transformed causal neuroscience and physiology and that the channelrhodopsin discovery plus its neuronal implementation is conceptually clean.
responses.response: I accept that optogenetics has changed experimental practice more than almost any recent method, and that maturity is not an issue. But six credible claimants for three slots, including Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, make any trio contestable, and direct patient benefit is still limited to early retinal work. I would not pair it with GLP-1 as a second part. As a methods prize it needs a clearly defensible attribution before it can pass, and I do not think we have one yet.

responses.point: Placed the unfolded protein response (B041, Walter and Mori) third as a conceptually original signalling discovery with a natural two-person attribution, while acknowledging the medical link is more indirect.
responses.response: I agree the Walter and Mori attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and the cell biology is outstanding. The question is the Medicine half of the prize. Therapeutic modulation of the UPR remains unproven, so it is a strong basic discovery that is not yet matched by clinical consequences. I rank it below the candidates with proven patient benefit, but I regard it as a serious future prize and would favour it over the cGAS-STING pathway on maturity and attribution.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen should displace Mojsov, or Habener should be considered, given that the credited list is incomplete and Mojsov's contribution is contested.
Whether CAR-T (B039) is better configured as June and Sadelain alone or with Rosenberg, and how Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work should weigh on fairness.
Whether the committee prefers a single GLP-1 prize or a shared prize that pairs it with a second achievement; the limit of three people makes the pairing costly for GLP-1.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted ballot. My documented spatial transcriptomics and single-cell work is not among the shortlisted achievements, and my co-authorship with Rickard Sandberg and others in the profile does not involve any credited candidate.
